meta.orientation: every pair is [A, B] in backtest.json order (A = first ufcstats name); p_* = probability that A wins
meta.open: first line BFO lists for the fight (one book, often weeks out; may not have been bettable in size)
meta.close: consensus closing line (decimal odds [A, B] = mean over books, then American): (1) mean of >= 3 US sportsbooks' closes on the BFO event page after dropping any book whose no-vig p is > 0.15 from the median book; (2) BFO's mean-odds series end point (mean of the books BFO tracked, read from both fighter pages) when the closing range is clean (spread <= 0.20); (3) 1-2 US books; (4) decimal midpoint of a clean closing range (nlbair); (5) one book's close (Ultimate UFC Dataset) when its overround is 0.99-1.15. `src` says which
meta.close_range: [[A low, A high], [B low, B high]] closing range across books (BFO), American
meta.cleaning: a closing range wider than 0.20 in implied probability holds a stale or in-play price that leaks the result; such ranges and BFO means are not used (eval.cleaning)
meta.books: per-book closing lines [A, B] (American) from BFO event pages; covers only the US books BFO lists today (about 2021 on)
meta.exchanges: Kalshi and Polymarket prices on BFO past-event pages are left out of market.json and the consensus: Kalshi's recorded last price scores log loss 0.33 vs 0.62 for the consensus on the same 2026 fights, i.e. it was captured after the result (eval.per_book); they stay in data/raw/odds/bfo_event_lines.csv
meta.walk_forward: closing lines are known only minutes before the fight; they are a benchmark and a stacking input for live use, never a feature of a model scored on the same fight before the line closes
sources: BestFightOdds.com (opening lines, closing ranges, mean-odds series, per-book closes), fetched by tools/market.py
nlbair/ufc-data v0.1.1 (CC BY 4.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23458636): BFO opening line and closing range per ufcstats fight id
Ultimate UFC Dataset (mdabbert / shortlikeafox, CC BY 4.0): one closing moneyline per fighter
meta.p_market_rating: walk-forward pre-fight probability from the market rating (Kalman filter on earlier closing lines and results; eval.market_rating has the equations and parameters); usable before any line exists
meta.ratings: current market ratings by fighters.json slug: [mu (log-odds), sd, last fight date, fights seen]
meta.p_market_rating_adj: p_market_rating plus the tune-fit offsets the closing line adds beyond the rating: logit += c_up (up_A - up_B) + c_down (down_A - down_B) + c_age (age_A - age_B) / 5; coefficients in eval.market_rating.adj_coef
meta.method6: market method-of-victory distribution [A_KO, A_SUB, A_DEC, B_KO, B_SUB, B_DEC]: per book the six "wins by TKO/KO / submission / decision" closing prices (decision = UD + split/majority when missing), power-normalised to sum 1, averaged over US books; KO includes doctor stoppages
meta.p_dec: P(fight goes to decision): two-way "goes to decision" prop, multiplicative no-vig, averaged over books
meta.round_dist: P(fight ends in round 1..K, decision), from "fight ends in round k" and "goes to decision" yes prices, power-normalised, averaged over books

UFC Fight Night: Vettori vs. Cannonier

cleaning.rule: closing range spread (implied-probability gap between low and high price of a side) > 0.2 marks the range and BFO mean as contaminated; per-book lines more than 0.15 from the median book are dropped

close_minus_rating.what: OLS of logit(p_close) - logit(p_rating) on A-minus-B features, no intercept; fit on tune
